eventMetadata.context_description: In Game 1 of the Western Conference semifinals, the sixth-seeded Timberwolves pulled off a stunning 104-102 road upset over the second-seeded Spurs, with Anthony Edwards returning from a knee injury off the bench under minutes restrictions, while Victor Wembanyama posted a near triple-double despite the loss. Heading into Game 2 at Frost Bank Center, Edwards remains questionable on the official injury report, tilting trader consensus heavily toward San Antonio (around 76% implied probability) amid their 62-20 regular-season dominance, home-court edge, and urgency for a bounce-back. Rudy Gobert's rim protection versus Wembanyama's versatility defines the paint battle, with Spurs rookie Carter Bryant also questionable; Minnesota's first-round win over Denver in six adds upset intrigue, but schedule rest favors the hosts.

eventMetadata.context_description: Trader consensus on Polymarket favors California Governor Gavin Newsom at 24.8% implied probability for the 2028 Democratic presidential nomination, driven by his national profile from recent book tours in early primary states like New Hampshire and perceived electability against Republican frontrunners in head-to-head polls. Former Vice President Kamala Harris trails at 8.4% despite leading some April surveys (e.g., McLaughlin showing her at 29%) after stating she's "thinking about" another run, weighed down by her 2024 general election loss. Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez holds 8.1% on progressive appeal and youth poll strength, while Sen. Jon Ossoff (6.7%) benefits from Georgia swing-state credentials. The fragmented field could consolidate around 2026 midterm performers, fundraising leaders, or those gaining key endorsements ahead of primaries.
